snapshot.title: SSC Science: Biology — Vitamins & Nutrition
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ SSC Biology Hook: KEDA: Fat. B,C: Water. A: Retinol. C: Scurvy. D: Sun/Rickets. K: Clot. B12: Cobalt. Iron: Anemia.

quick_notes.title: Fat Soluble Vitamins
quick_notes.detail: A (Retinol - Night Blindness), D (Calciferol - Rickets), E (Tocopherol - Fertility), K (Phylloquinone - Blood Clotting). (Mnemonic: KEDA).
quick_notes.explanation: Fat soluble vitamins are vitamins that dissolve in fat and can be stored in the body's fatty tissues. There are four fat soluble vitamins: vitamin A, also called retinol, and a lack of it causes night blindness, which is trouble seeing in dim light; vitamin D, also called calciferol, and a lack of it causes rickets, which is soft and weak bones in children; vitamin E, also called tocopherol, and a lack of it can cause fertility problems; and vitamin K, also called phylloquinone, and a lack of it causes trouble with blood clotting, meaning bleeding does not stop easily. To remember these four vitamins in order, you can use the mnemonic KEDA, which stands for K, E, D, A.

quick_notes.title: Water Soluble Vitamins
quick_notes.detail: B-complex (B1 Thiamine - Beri Beri, B12 Cobalt - Anemia), C (Ascorbic Acid - Scurvy).
quick_notes.explanation: Water soluble vitamins dissolve in water and are not stored in the body, so you need to get them from food regularly. The B-complex group includes many vitamins, such as vitamin B1, also called thiamine, and a lack of it causes a disease called beriberi. Another B vitamin is vitamin B12, also called cobalamin, and not having enough can lead to anemia, which is a condition where your blood cannot carry enough oxygen. Vitamin C, also known as ascorbic acid, is another water soluble vitamin, and a deficiency causes scurvy, a disease that makes you feel weak and causes bleeding gums.

quick_notes.title: Important Minerals
quick_notes.detail: Iron (Hemoglobin/Anemia), Calcium (Bones/Teeth), Iodine (Thyroid/Goitre), Fluorine (Dental decay if in excess).
quick_notes.explanation: Iron is a mineral that helps your body make hemoglobin, which is the part of red blood cells that carries oxygen, and not having enough iron can cause anemia, a condition where you feel tired and weak. Calcium is a mineral that builds strong bones and teeth, and a lack of calcium can lead to weak or brittle bones. Iodine is a mineral needed by your thyroid gland, which is a small organ in your neck that controls your body's energy use, and without enough iodine you can develop goitre, an enlargement of the thyroid. Fluorine is a mineral that helps prevent tooth decay, but having too much fluorine can actually cause dental fluorosis, which damages tooth enamel and leads to decay.

quick_notes.title: Macronutrients
quick_notes.detail: Carbohydrates (Energy), Proteins (Body building), Fats (Storage). 1g Fat : 9 kcal (Highest).
quick_notes.explanation: Macronutrients are the nutrients your body needs in large amounts to function properly, and they include carbohydrates, proteins, and fats. Carbohydrates are the body's main source of energy, meaning they give you fuel to move and think. Proteins help build and repair body tissues like muscles, skin, and organs. Fats are used for long-term energy storage and also protect your organs. Each gram of fat provides 9 kilocalories, which is more than double the energy given by a gram of carbohydrate or protein, making fat the most energy-dense macronutrient.

quick_notes.title: Quick Facts
quick_notes.detail: Vitamin D is synthesized by skin in sunlight. Vitamin B12 contains Cobalt. Vitamin C is lost on boiling.
quick_notes.explanation: Vitamin D is a nutrient that your body makes when your skin is exposed to sunlight, so you do not need to get it from food. Vitamin B12 is a nutrient that contains the metal cobalt, which is essential for its structure and function. Vitamin C is a nutrient that gets destroyed when you boil food or water that contains it, so eating raw fruits and vegetables helps you get enough of it.
